reasoning: Pepper plant (Capsicum) showing sudden collapse of a single branch/leaf with water-soaked, brown, drooping tissue while the rest of the plant remains healthy and green. This is the classic presentation of Phytophthora capsici blight on pepper — rapid branch wilt and water-soaked necrosis without white fuzzy sporulation, distinguishing it from late blight. No white mycelium, spots, halos, or concentric rings that would indicate other diseases.
